speaker: margery_pell
text: I have it already, off the stair. People talking before they paid me. Two hundred, if I am to put one figure on it. I did not stand in the road and count coats.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Two hundred. I will say it as she said it. I do not have a second count, and I will not invent one to keep her company.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: I had apprentices and one man carried, and a gate. That is what a boy told me at the door. It is not two hundred. He did not give me a number I will swear to.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Your boy saw what was in front of his nose. The stair heard the people who had been behind him. I am not marrying the two stories. I am telling you the figure I have.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Then we have two figures and one agreement, if we can find the agreement. I have not found it in the numbers.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: What do the two stories both say? Not the number. The thing you both saw, or both were told.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: People running toward the noise. That much the boy said, and he was out of breath from doing it.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: People running toward the noise. I will agree to that sentence. I will not agree to a number of my own, and I will not agree to two hundred, except as Margery's figure and not as mine.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Two hundred is mine. Let it stay mine. I don't like a morning when the stair arrives already talking about a gate.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: Then someone should go down and see which story is true. The gate is on the way we walk. It is not a pilgrimage.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: No. I have been past it. I saw the gate open, the hasp wrenched, a cap in the road, and backs running north. I did not see a man brought out. I am not going back to collect the version that flatters a walk.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Not going down. I can write that without a figure beside it. It is the cleanest line we have had this morning.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Stay up here, then. I have a stair to keep, and a play at two, and I will not have my gatherers turned into messengers.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: I think we ought to know. I will say so once, and I will not make it a quarrel. If you will not, I will not go alone and call it the company's errand.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Don't go alone. Don't go for me. The road can settle its own story without a player in it to bring a better one home.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Agreed, and agreed only to the running. People were running toward the noise. Two hundred is hers. His boy gave him a gate and a man, and no count. The gate you saw yourself. That is the list. I am not adding a line under it.

speaker: margery_pell
text: Good. Pay me no more attention until the afternoon, unless you are paying me money. Two hundred is the talk. It is not a receipt.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we have a play to rehearse, and a street that will go on making noises whether we cast them or not.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: I will rehearse. I do not like leaving a story in two shapes. I will leave it, because you said no, and not because the two shapes became one.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: Two shapes, left as two. I can copy that. I will not copy a third we did not hear.

speaker: margery_pell
text: And you will not hear a third from me. Two hundred. The stair. My money-box is a different box, and it is not open yet.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep them separate. I will not have a stair's figure walked down to the gate to see if the gate agrees.

speaker: richard_cowley
text: Then I am done asking. A gate and a man was what I was told. I will not improve it by walking.

speaker: humphrey_larkham
text: People running toward the noise. I am saying it once more, so the morning has one sentence it can keep.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Keep that one. The rest stays with the person who brought it.
